title: De Jong Sidelined for Months as Barcelona Fumes at Dutch Team Over Knee Injury
excerpt: FC Barcelona confirmed captain Frenkie de Jong has a torn medial collateral ligament in his right knee sustained during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, with the club furious at the Netherlands' handling of the injury during the tournament.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • De Jong faces a five-to-six-month recovery from a torn MCL, risking the entire first half of the season.
  • Barcelona is furious with the Dutch team's medical staff for allowing De Jong to play injured during the World Cup.
  • Surgery is currently avoided, but Barcelona prefers it to prevent future knee issues.
  • De Jong insists he was committed to Barcelona, claiming initial assessments deemed his injury minor.

FC Barcelona confirmed on Thursday that captain Frenkie de Jong has suffered a tear of the medial collateral ligament (MCL) in his right knee, an injury sustained during the Netherlands' 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign. The 29-year-old midfielder faces an estimated five to six months on the sidelines, according to journalist Javi Miguel of AS, potentially ruling him out for the entire first half of the 2026-27 La Liga season.

https://x.com/Footballtweet/status/2080579238273450406

"Tests carried out on first-team player Frenkie de Jong have determined that he is suffering from a tear in the medial collateral ligament of his right knee," the club stated. "It has been agreed that the player will continue under medical treatment and monitoring, pending his progress over the coming weeks."

Barcelona Furious With Netherlands

The diagnosis has triggered a bitter fallout between Barcelona and the Royal Netherlands Football Association. According to Catalunya Radio, relations between the club and the player have also deteriorated, with internal friction mounting over how the injury was managed during the World Cup.

Barcelona officials are reportedly furious with head coach Ronald Koeman and his staff. "The anger within the club is monumental, as they believe there was negligence on the part of all those responsible, to the point that he played injured in the match against Morocco with the approval of the coach and doctors," Diario AS reported.

De Jong played through the knockout rounds with heavy bandaging and painkilling injections — a medical approach that Barcelona's staff believe compromised his long-term physical stability. The Netherlands were eliminated in the round of 32 following a penalty shootout loss to Morocco, according to Reuters.

De Jong Breaks His Silence

Hours after the club's medical update, De Jong published a lengthy statement on Instagram addressing growing speculation about both his injury and his dedication to Barcelona.

"During the World Cup I suffered a knee injury. After the first assessments, the doctors told me it was a minor injury and that it was not getting worse as I continued playing. During my holidays I returned to Barcelona for further tests. Those showed that the injury was more serious than initially determined."

— Frenkie de Jong, via Instagram

The Dutch international pushed back against questions about his commitment: "It is difficult for me to see people questioning my relationship with and commitment to the club because of false information. Football means everything to me, and I have always given everything I have for FC Barcelona and for my country."

Treatment Divide and Squad Impact

While Barcelona's official statement confirmed conservative treatment, reports suggest a divide between the club and De Jong's camp. According to Catalunya Radio, Barcelona is pushing for immediate surgery to resolve underlying chronic instability in the knee joint and prevent future relapses, while the player's representatives have traditionally favored non-invasive recovery methods.

A final decision on the treatment pathway was expected on Friday following specialized medical tests at the Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper training complex.

De Jong's absence deals a significant blow to head coach Hansi Flick's planning ahead of the new campaign. Barcelona, chasing a third consecutive La Liga title, open their season with a visit to Elche on August 23. Pedri, Gavi, Marc Bernal, Dani Olmo, and Fermin Lopez are all expected to shoulder greater midfield responsibility during the captain's absence, according to OneFootball.

De Jong has now missed more than 400 days through injuries during his seven-year spell at Barcelona. This latest setback adds an estimated 150 days to that total, taking it to well over a year and a half of cumulative time lost.

What's Next

Barcelona's medical team will continue monitoring De Jong's recovery in the coming weeks, with the conservative-versus-surgical debate likely to be resolved after Friday's final assessment. For the La Liga champions, the priority is clear: ensure a full recovery rather than rush the captain back to a midfield that must now adapt without one of its most influential figures through at least the end of 2026.
